sentences.text:
Dr. C. Rajasekar vs State Rep. By The Inspector Of Police on 8
January, 2025
Bench: Vikram Nath, Sanjay Karol

In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction

Criminal Appeal No(S). Of 2025
 (Arising From Slp (Criminal) No(S). 371/2020)
 Dr. C. Rajasekar ... Appellant(S)
 Versus
 State Rep. By The ... Respondent(S)
 Inspector Of Police
O R D E R Leave granted 2.
The appellant was acquitted by the Sessions Court and the High Court has reversed the acquittal and recorded conviction under Section 498A of the IPC with one year sentence of simple imprisonment.
The fine amount of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs only) has already been paid to the wife.
3. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the State.

4. The impugned order reflects that no finding has been recorded by the High Court to the effect that the view taken by the Sessions Court was not a possible view and only upon re-appreciation without such finding, the conviction has been recorded.
5. We further take note of the fact that the marriage between the parties has already been dissolved and the fine amount has already been paid.

As such, we are inclined to set aside the impugned order dated 16th August, 2019 in Criminal Appeal No. 217 of 2011 and restore that of the Sessions Court passed on 18th December, 2009 in Criminal Appeal No. 185 of 2006 acquitting the appellant.
It is ordered accordingly.
